title: Douglas v. Deutsche Bank National Trust Co. — firm pressed on supervision of AI-drafted filing
text: Published order addressing a brief containing fabricated authority. The firm attributed the conduct to a former employee and did not describe its supervision or review of the work, acknowledging only that 'further review should have been undertaken.' Court treats AI risk as no longer creditable as unknown and catalogues the duties: validate AI output, consider disclosure or client consent, protect confidences, adopt firm-wide policy, bill ethically.

title: Capital Standard v. US Bank National Association — 31 further mis-cites after amended brief
text: Counsel used generative AI in an appeal with no apparent safeguards. The original brief carried nonexistent quotations; the amended brief added at least 31 more instances of real cases quoted inaccurately or cited for propositions they do not support, including a fabricated quotation attributed to a Florida Supreme Court case. Show-cause order issued 2026-01-08.

title: Bray v. Griner Investments, Inc. — standing order requires signed AI-use disclosure in every pleading [trial court — confirm tier]
text: Because of increased AI use by unrepresented parties, the court ORDERS that all pleadings, including any amended complaint, carry a signed statement disclosing whether AI was used to help prepare or draft the pleading, and certifying that the accuracy of all facts and legal authorities has been verified. The filer need not explain how AI was used. Non-compliance may draw sanctions including dismissal. This is a court mandating up-front disclosure, against the Illinois item on this line holding disclosure is NOT required.

title: Michael L Ruiz v. Magellan Financial & Insurance Services — counsel ordered to show cause over false quotations [trial court — confirm tier]
text: Court holds a lawyer may not make a legal argument without good faith basis in law, and that the duty of candor is implicated by unchecked use of generative tools known to be unreliable. No finding of intentional conduct is required to impose serious discipline for misrepresentations to the court. Counsel ordered to show cause within 14 days why she should not be sanctioned or disciplined for false quotations.

title: Alcon Entertainment v. Tesla / Musk — protective order requires advance AI Disclosures naming vendor and tool version [trial court — confirm tier]
text: Protected material may not be uploaded to any GenAI or LLM tool, third-party, public or internal. The sole exception is a closed litigation or case-management tool that does not share data outside the instance where the document sits. Before using even that, the receiving party must give advance notice and provide 'AI Disclosures': vendor name, tool name and version, and technical information on functionality, security, and data exposure. The producing party may object, and material cannot go to the tool until the court resolves a dispute. Protected material may never touch an open or public tool.

title: Myles v. State Farm General Insurance — Secure AI environments required; public ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini named as prohibited [trial court — confirm tier]
text: Protected material and information derived from it may not be uploaded into any open, public, or non-secure AI tool, including large language models, unless the tool gives verifiable technical and contractual assurances of privacy, security, and no training or incorporation into other systems. Use is allowed only in 'Secure AI' environments: closed, limited to persons with equivalent confidentiality duties, and protected by reasonable safeguards. Public versions of ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are listed as prohibited examples. Unauthorized access or a security incident involving AI must be promptly reported and mitigated.

title: DIRECTV v. NexStar Media Group — submitting protected material to an open AI tool counts as third-party disclosure [trial court — confirm tier]
text: Protected Material may not be submitted to any open generative AI tool, such as ChatGPT, or similar public tools; doing so counts as disclosure to a third party under the order. Receiving parties must store and use protected material securely, notify the producing party promptly of any loss, breach, or suspected unauthorized access with enough information to assess scope, and take corrective action.

title: 5000 PLUS LLC v. Majestic Steel USA — order defines open and closed AI systems for discovery use [trial court — confirm tier]
text: Order permits AI use for drafting, discovery processing, summarizing, organizing and document review provided it complies with Rule 11 and applicable duties. Protected Material may be used with a closed AI system only where the user has a good-faith basis to believe the system does not train publicly accessible models on submitted materials and restricts access consistent with the order. Open AI systems may be used only where Protected Material is not disclosed in violation of the order. Defines both terms and cross-references the judge's standing order ban on uploading sealed documents.

title: Ibrahim v. Apple Inc. — protective order requires a recognized security framework (ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, CIS v8) [trial court — confirm tier]
text: Receiving party must use an information security management system with reasonable administrative, physical and technical safeguards, network security and encryption, meeting at least one recognized cybersecurity framework such as ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, or CIS Critical Security Controls v8. Names a vendor-attestation-grade standard as the condition of handling protected material.
